widget.solution:
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

def closes_chart(days, closes):
    fig, ax = plt.subplots()
    ax.plot(days, closes)
    # title, x label and y label
    ax.set_title("Harbour closes")
    ax.set_xlabel("Day")
    ax.set_ylabel("Close (£)")
    return ax

screens.title: A number with no unit
screens.prose: Another chart, of Wren plc, has no y label. Its last close reads 404.10. You hold 1,000 Wren shares, and many London shares are quoted in pence.
screens.question: What is the holding worth?

screens.title: Pounds on the ticks
screens.prose:
A tick formatter writes the unit on every tick.

```python
from matplotlib.ticker import StrMethodFormatter
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(StrMethodFormatter("£{x:,.2f}"))
```

It fills `{x}` with each tick's value, using Python's format rules.
screens.question: What does the tick at 1250 read?

options.why: `,` adds the thousands separator and `.2f` keeps two decimal places. Both are in the pattern.
The formatter fills `{x}` with the tick value. The braces never appear on the chart.
The `£` comes first in the pattern, so it comes first on the tick.

hints.text: Fill `{x}` with 1250 and apply `,.2f`.
`,` groups thousands with commas; `.2f` gives two decimal places.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Work through the pattern from left to right.

byKey.nosep: The pattern has `,` and `.2f`, so the tick gets a comma and two decimal places: £1,250.00.

explain.text: `StrMethodFormatter` runs `"£{x:,.2f}".format(x=1250)` for each tick. The `,` adds the comma and `.2f` the pence. Every tick now carries the unit, so no reader has to guess.

screens.title: A readable chart
screens.prose:
Name every line, say what the chart shows, and give each axis its quantity and unit.

```python
ax.plot(days, harbour, label="Harbour")
ax.plot(days, osprey, label="Osprey")
ax.set_title("Closing prices")
ax.set_xlabel("Day")
ax.set_ylabel("Close (£)")
fmt = StrMethodFormatter("£{x:,.2f}")
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(fmt)
ax.legend()
```

widget.solution:
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.ticker import StrMethodFormatter

def value_chart(days, values):
    fig, ax = plt.subplots()
    ax.plot(days, values)
    ax.set_title("Portfolio value")
    ax.set_xlabel("Day")
    ax.set_ylabel("Value (£)")
    ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(StrMethodFormatter("£{x:,.0f}"))
    return ax
